messages:
Maya: Quick sync: we're launching the new Runtime Health dashboard next week. It combines runtime + infra inputs (GPU contention, queue latency, batch efficiency, KV cache hit, and SLO burn rate). Need alignment on alert rules, thresholds, and pager routing. Primary asks: 1) recommended thresholds per metric (suggested baseline), 2) non-actionable noise suppression (sustained windows, dedupe), 3) which teams get paged for which alerts and escalation order, and 4) runbook links. Can folks chime in with concrete rule examples?

Arjun: +1. My high-level: group alerts into Sev1 (customer-impacting SLO burn or service unavailable), Sev2 (degraded but not blocking), and warnings (ops-only, dashboard-visible). For SLO burn use sustained windows to avoid flapping. Example rule (Prometheus-style):

```
ALERT HighSLOBurn
  IF slo_burn_rate_5m > 1.5
  FOR 10m
  LABELS { severity="sev1" }
  ANNOTATIONS { summary="SLO burn > 1.5 for 10m", runbook="https://redwood/runbooks/slo-burn" }
```

Arjun: Also recommend route-scoped labels (model, route, customer_tier). Page on sev1 only if burn persisted >10m and token loss > 1% of baseline. Otherwise send to #platform-ops and ticket.

Lina: On instrumentation: runtime will emit `batch_efficiency`, `kv_cache_hit_ratio`, `queue_latency_p95`, `gpu_utilization_90` and `slo_burn_rate_5m` with labels {route, model, region}. We can add customer_tier if product tags are available. For batch efficiency, threshold below 0.6 for 5m should trigger warning; below 0.4 for 15m is sev2 (because it implies cost spike + latency).

Ben: Paging notes: prefer a single pager for Sev1 -> eng-sre primary oncall (PD key: PD_SRE_RUNTIME). If not acknowledged in 5m escalate to eng-runtime (PD_RUNTIME_TEAM). After 15m escalate to eng-platform/product owner. For Sev2 go to #platform-ops slack channel and create a ticket (no immediate page). Ops runbook link: https://redwood/runbooks/runtime-pager.

Priya: UX/Console: dashboard will show alerts inline and allow quick suppress/ack. We should add alert metadata: owners, runbook, playbook snippet, and actionable next steps. Also please include `suppress_for` heuristics (e.g., maintenance windows, canary rollouts). For rollout windows, automatically suppress non-sev1 alerts if `rollout_in_progress=true` label present.

Arjun: Agree on suppression. Also propose dedupe heuristics on route label to avoid multi-pages when multiple nodes show same problem. Alertmanager route example snippet: 

```yaml
route:
  receiver: "pd-sev1"
  group_by: ["route","model"]
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 5m
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
    - match:
        severity: "sev1"
      receiver: "pd-sre-runtime"
      continue: false
```

Lina: Small note on metrics: `slo_burn_rate_5m` should be derived from request-level success/failure and token counts. We'll need a consistent cardinality strategy (route+region, avoid model_hash). I'll add a PR for export naming and labels.

Maya: For thresholds, propose we start with these baselines and iterate:
- SLO burn (5m): warn >1.2, sev1 >1.5 sustained 10m
- Queue latency p95: warn >250ms, sev2 >500ms sustained 10m
- Batch efficiency: warn <0.6 (5m), sev2 <0.4 (15m)
- KV cache hit ratio: warn <0.7, sev2 <0.5
- GPU util 90th: warn >85% w/ sustained queuing, sev2 if >95% and queuing present

Maya: Can eng-sre own the initial alerting rules + Alertmanager routes? Eng-runtime to add labels and confirm metric names. Eng-platform will wire dashboard links + runbooks and coordinate sim/DR tests.

Arjun: I can draft the first set of alert rules and route config. Will push a PR to infra/alerts and @Ben please verify PD escalation keys.

Ben: I will validate PD keys and update paging policy. Also recommend test playbook run: trigger a synthetic slo_burn spike in staging and ensure paging -> ack -> escalation works.

Priya: I'll add the runbooks to the dashboard annotations and wire an "Acknowledge" button that triggers Alertmanager silence via API. Also will add a toggle to hide warnings during canary rollouts.

OpsBot: New dashboard created: https://console.redwood/dashboards/runtime-health (owner: eng-platform) :white_check_mark:

Lina: I'll open the instrumentation PR today (link to follow). One ask: include `customer_tier=enterprise|standard|free` label if available so we can route enterprise incidents to account ops when appropriate.

Arjun: We'll add a severity label mapping that factors in customer_tier: if enterprise + sev2 -> page on-call sooner (escalate after 3m). Add to the routing logic.

Maya: Thanks everyone. Next actions: Arjun PR with rules (target: tomorrow EOD), Lina PR for metric labels (today), Ben update PD escalation (EOD), Priya add runbooks and UI hooks (this week). We'll test in staging Thursday. If anyone has objections to thresholds above speak now. :eyes:

Ben: no objections, sounds good.

Priya: ok from UX side.

Arjun: filing PR now -> https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4523

Lina: instrumentation PR -> https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2101

Maya: Great, I'll keep the rollout checklist updated. Thanks! :raised_hands:
